brief.scope: adversarial-review of lane/session-20260916-h against origin/dev: records only. Read ops/conductor/harness-capabilities.md (the two 2026-09-16 rows), ops/conductor/handoff/probes/probes-2026-09-16-classifier-edge.jsonl, .claude/skills/refused/SKILL.md (the classifier row), CONTRIB.md (the ready table's new row), and the six briefs under ops/conductor/handoff/briefs-2026-09-16-classes/. Hunt: a claim without its reading; a measurement misread (the matcher regex in .claude/settings.json, the vendor doc's Match MCP tools section); a probe row that passes on a wrong tree or fails on a right one; a brief whose mechanism leaves its failure class reachable (a second LD-68 on one host; a lock reading differing between two show calls; a wrapper test touching a host path; a ready flip without a closed audit at the head); rows that do not execute the subject; contradictions with docs/tests.md, ops/process/pipeline.md, the state skill. Quote both halves of every finding.

findings.claim: declared (harness-capabilities.md §Claude Code, MEASURED 2026-09-16 at 46639344): ".claude/settings.json matches the engine and the matrix on PreToolUse to Write\|Edit\|MultiEdit\|mcp__serena__(replace\|insert\|rename\|safe_delete).*, so the four serena write tools are seen and no other server's tool is; no matcher spells mcp__.*". Vendor half quoted in the same cell: "a bare mcp__memory is an exact string and matches nothing". practiced (code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks §Matcher patterns / §Match MCP tools): "Only letters, digits, _, -, spaces, ,, and | — Exact string, or list of exact strings separated by | or ,"; "Contains any other character — JavaScript regular expression, unanchored"; "RegExp.prototype.test ... succeeds on a match anywhere in the value. Edit.* matches both Edit and NotebookEdit"; "The .* is required: a matcher like mcp__memory ... is compared as an exact string and matches no tool". practiced (.claude/settings.json:57 and :108): matcher Write|Edit|MultiEdit|mcp__serena__(replace|insert|rename|safe_delete).* contains (), . and *, so the whole value is unanchored regex. misses: Write|Edit|MultiEdit alone would have been exact names; the serena groups and .* put Edit on the unanchored path (NotebookEdit matches) and Write on it (mcp__other__WriteFile matches). Absence of the literal mcp__.* does not mean no other server's tool is seen.

declared (P-CLS-20260916-serena-matcher): question "Which MCP tools do the engine and the matrix see on PreToolUse today, by the settings matcher?"; serve "rg -c -F 'mcp__serena__(replace|insert|rename|safe_delete).*' .claude/settings.json"; expect "2". practiced: that literal is one PreToolUse matcher shared by matrix.py and engine.py (.claude/settings.json:57) and a second PostToolUse matcher on ruff-after-edit.sh (:108), not a second PreToolUse engine/matrix matcher. rg -c prints 2 and the row PASSes. A tree with only the claimed PreToolUse object prints 1 (FAIL on a right tree). A tree with the matcher deleted: rg -c exits 1 and probes.py run_row treats nonzero serve as UNREACHABLE, not FAIL. stdout 12 contains expect 2 (PASS on a wrong tree). misses: the row never pins PreToolUse, never pins engine.py/matrix.py, and cannot fail a missing matcher.
findings.reproduce: rg -n -F 'mcp__serena__(replace|insert|rename|safe_delete).*' .claude/settings.json; rg -c -F 'mcp__serena__(replace|insert|rename|safe_delete).*' .claude/settings.json; echo EXIT:$?; rg -c -F 'mcp__NOT_A_REAL_PATTERN_xyz' .claude/settings.json; echo NOMATCH_EXIT:$?

findings.claim: declared (S2 opening measurement at 46639344): "python3 ops/conductor/tools/defects.py next on the main checkout prints LD-68 while two branches already carry LD-68.md; a third is one command away". declared (S2 mechanism): "two sessions on one host read one highest and mint one id. The fix is a host-local reservation taken in one transaction, so two owners cannot hold one number" and "highest() keeps its bounded fetch of origin/<trunk>". practiced (ops/conductor/tools/ledger.py:147-176): highest is still "the working tree and on origin/<trunk>" only; sibling-branch files never enter that max. practiced (S2 Not covered): "The two LD-68s already filed, reconciled by hand before either PR merges". misses: ledger_reservations starts empty and does not import unmerged LD-68.md; after this mechanism, next on a host whose origin/dev and current tree lack LD-68.md still prints LD-68 — the measured one-host class stays reachable until a hand reconcile the lever does not do.

findings.claim: declared (S3 Not covered): "The reason one legacy string read differently on two calls is not measured (the shape is removed rather than explained)". declared (issue 3): "lane/session-20260915-g's measure read unreachable (exit 1) and met on different show calls". practiced (S3 mechanism): "A target already stored as a string (every live target today) is read as legacy: run through shlex.split as now, and its target line says legacy-string". practiced (ops/conductor/tools/deliverable.py:111, unchanged on this ref): "proc = run(shlex.split(target['measure']), cwd=REPO_ROOT, timeout=MEASURE_TIMEOUT)". practiced (S3 mechanism, bare vs named show): "Bare show prints ... reading not run"; "show <branch> runs that one measure". misses: the tokenizer class is kept for every live target; two show <branch> calls can still disagree on a legacy string; bare show and show <branch> now disagree by design.

declared (P-CLS-20260916-vendor-reading): "Where is the vendor's reading that MCP tools are matched like any other tool recorded, and at which harness version?" serve rg -c 'Match MCP tools' ops/conductor/harness-capabilities.md expect 1. declared (P-CLS-20260916-classifier-not-a-hook): "The classifier's denial of hand.py declare is a hook row misfiring; which row in boundaries.json is it?" serve rg -c 'Self-Modification' ops/conductor/harness-capabilities.md expect 1. declared (P-CLS-20260916-audit-before-ready): "What must a PR's Proof section name before the PR is marked ready" serve rg -c 'gpt-daybreak-blue-latest' CONTRIB.md expect 1. practiced (docs/probes.md): serve passes when the expected substring is in stdout. practiced: each command greps the record for a phrase; none reads the vendor page, none reads boundaries.json, none reads a PR body or runs gh pr ready. misses: a tree that mentions the words without the vendor rule, without a boundaries.json correction, or without a closed audit at the head still PASSes.

findings.claim: declared (S5 Rows): "each executes the wrapper and asserts what it did". declared (host-store-untouched-by-construction): "the environment handed to the wrapper carries no path under the host's home (assert on the env dict, not on the host)". declared (jobs-root-under-world-state): "the host home path does not appear in the resolved argv or the record". practiced (docs/tests.md rule 4): "A world is hermetic by default; ambient is explicit and named." practiced (this ref, ops/conductor/tests/test_dispatch_wrapper.py:120-129): _jobs_roots_to_guard already names Path.home()/.../dispatch. misses: host-store-untouched-by-construction does not run the wrapper; hermeticity is still proved by reading a host path. A wrapper that writes through ~ with DISPATCH_JOBS unset stays green on the env-dict row.
